  ID:            01M768G9Q8B52KT14SS0GZP334
  Project:       gh/orin-dx
  Status:        open
  Phase:         planning
  URL:           https://entire.com/gh/orin-dx/-/trails/328
  Assignees:     ulid:01KY3576VGXBH5688NK9BQNC88
  Type:          task
  Priority:      low
  Created:       2026-11-11T21:33:57Z
  Last activity: 2026-11-12T05:05:28Z

Description:
Intent: found while fixing PR 423. The walkers (discover_files, discover_dirs) honour .gitignore and skip hidden files, but is_source_file (crates/core/src/pipeline/discover.rs; callers revision.rs ~513 and watch/lazy.rs ~280, used by the watcher's update_file) does not, so a changed path that is .gitignored (or hidden) is treated as a source file and extracted. One rule written twice with different inputs. Change: one function decides whether a path is a source file, used by the walkers and by is_source_file, with the ignore and hidden handling (the ignore crate's matchers) in it; keep it cheap per watcher event. Gate: a consistency test like the exclude one: discover_files, discover_dirs and is_source_file agree on gitignored and hidden paths; a watched session ignores a gitignored file's change; tests fail on main. Source: PR 423 worker report.

0027-identify-a-component-by-its-declaration-and-exports.md
# 0027. Identify a component by its declaration and its exports, not its display name

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-10 (accepted 2026-11-13, once implemented)

## Context

The extractor knows which declaration a component is and which names its module exports it under (`LexedExport::LocalDeclaration { name, declared_as }`, the attached sub-components in `extractor/uses.rs`). It keeps neither: `ComponentMapping` holds `component_name` and `exported: bool` (set by name), and `ComponentEntry` holds `display_name` and `exported`. Every reader that needs to know which export a component is works it out again from the display name:

- The checker backend takes the export named like the display name, or like its last `/` or `.` segment, else the module's `default` (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs`). With `Menu.Item = Item; export default Menu`, the checker run gives `Item` the props of `Menu` and reports it as resolved by the checker (reproduced with the CLI and tsrs 0.23.0: structural `Item` has `value`, checker `Item` has `label` and `open`).
- The merge and the session pair an answer with its entry by file and display name (the merge in `types/semantic.rs`, `pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`). A late answer takes the first component with no pairing at all (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`).
- The oracle matches by `normComponent` (`apps/oracle/src/tool-universe.ts`), which strips the path, the `.` prefix and every non-alphanumeric character, so `_Card` and `Card`, or `Menu.Item` and `Item`, are one name. A default and a named export of one function were counted twice (review finding on PR 413).
- The Storybook addon compares a story's import name with `displayName` and reads the module's exports with regular expressions (`packages/storybook/src/exports.ts`).
- The S5 probe prints a generic default as text and reads it in another module, where a module-local `FormData` becomes the DOM global (review finding on PR 410).

Each case was fixed, or is being fixed, in the reader where a review found it. The next reader starts from the display name again. After ADR 0026's S8 the checker's answer is the default output, so a wrong pairing is no longer confined to an opt-in path. The construct suite has one component per file (`Row`), so S7's gate cannot see one.

## Decision

A component's identity is its declaration and its exports. Its display name is for display and for addressing by a host; nothing pairs, dedupes or caches on it. Two identities serve two purposes, and each is named for its own:

- The extractor records each component's exports: the names its module exports it under (`default` included), or for an attached sub-component the path through its exports, which starts at the export name, not the parent's local name. `Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default.Item`. A reader maps `default` to its own import binding. `exported` is whether there are any.
- Pairing a checker answer with its entry is by output key: a request carries the key, the answer and each fallback carry it back, and the merge finds the entry by key. Dedupe is by declaration (file and span of the declaring node). The extractor does not record the span in its output yet; the oracle dedupes by declaration today (PR 413), and core does not. Across revisions the identity stays `ComponentId`, because spans move with edits.
- The checker backend asks for a recorded export by its exact name, follows aliases, and keeps the structural result with a reason when the export is missing or declared in another file. It never falls back to `default` unless `default` is a recorded export. A generic sub-component reached through a parent's property is not instantiated; it keeps the structural result with a reason.
- An attachment records which component it attaches by that component's own identity: `Local(name)` for a module binding, `Inline(span_start)` for an inline function with no binding. Nothing re-finds a mapping by display name, so `A.Item = …` beside `B.Item = …` stay two components.
- The canonical JSON gives each component its `exports`. Readers outside the crate (oracle, addon, scripts) join on file and export name and stop re-deriving names. Until part 2 (trail 302) `ComponentEntry` keeps `exported` beside `exports`, and `exports` is not serialized.
- A type argument written into a probe resolves to the declaration the checker read it from: it is either written in the declaring module or checked against that declaration. Printed text is not re-read in another scope unchecked.

## Consequences

- `SourceData` changes, so `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` moves (ADR 0003). The canonical JSON gains a field, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` moves from 6 to 7 with the oracle's `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION`, the TypeScript declarations and the `schema` command (ADR 0017). `SemanticTarget`, `SemanticComponent` and `SemanticFallback` are public in `caliper-docgen-core`, so the core crate takes a minor bump.
- The checker's symbol handle names a declaration by node index, kind and path, not by offset, so the backend checks the file, not the span. It compares the file against the module symbol's own declaration path, not a path the host built, because the checker lowercases paths on macOS. A span check would need a request this audit did not find in the protocol.
- The construct suite gains rows with several components in one file: a default and a named export of one function, `export { _X as X }`, an attached sub-component beside a default export, and a default export beside a named one. They gate this change and S7.
- This lands before S7. S7 deletes most of the structural resolver, where the remaining name-capture findings live (ADR 0025 owns those until then); the extractor's candidate and export detection stays, and this decision is about that part.
- A host that addresses a component by display name keeps working: `component_in` stays, and a lookup by export is added beside it.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep the display name and fix each reader: five readers so far, each fixed alone, each with its own normalization.
- Key on the checker's symbol handle: it lives in one snapshot of one checker (ADR 0026 rules out keying on checker ids), and the structural path and the hosts never see it.
- Key on the span across revisions: it moves with every edit above the component, which is why `ComponentId` uses the name and an ordinal.

`WatchSession` (`pipeline/watch.rs`) holds one immutable `Revision` in an `ArcSwapOption` and a writer `Mutex`. `initialize()` builds the first revision with `Revision::cold()` and is idempotent; `rebuild()` replaces it with a fresh cold one. `update_file(changed)` takes the writer lock, builds the next revision with `Revision::next()`, and publishes it with one atomic store. Readers (`snapshot()`) never wait on the writer and always see one complete revision.

`ensure_fresh()` is for a host without a file watcher. Under the writer lock it compares stamps (modification time and size, plus a content hash while the time is within 2 s of the stat) of the revision's source files, every directory discovery walks, and every resolution config. A changed config rebuilds; a changed directory reruns discovery to find created and deleted files; each changed file goes through `Revision::next()` in path order. It returns one `output_delta()` from the starting output to the final one. Stamps are recorded on the first call after a cold extraction, and anything modified within 2 s of that extraction's start counts as changed, so an edit made while it ran is not lost.

`Revision::next(changed)`:

1. Ignores a path discovery would not include (outside every source directory, excluded, not TypeScript): `discover::is_source_file`.
2. Re-parses `changed` into copies of the previous global data and named-type index. A missing file is a deletion; any other read error (permissions, invalid UTF-8) declares nothing and records an `IoError`, exactly as a cold run does.
3. With `load_dependencies`, loads only the demands of `changed` the session's layer has not followed (`DependencyLayer::missing`) into a new layer built on the previous one's parsed files and answers, so a new package import costs one load and an unchanged one none.
4. Re-resolves the components that are new, live in `changed`, or whose recorded dependencies the change touches (below). Every other component keeps its previous `Arc<Resolved>`.
5. Calls `assemble()`, then reports the delta against the previous revision's output: `updated_keys` (re-resolved components, and kept ones whose key moved when a same-named component elsewhere appeared or disappeared), `removed_keys`, and the diagnostics added and removed. Applying every delta in revision order to the first snapshot yields the current snapshot; `every_kind_of_change_leaves_the_snapshot_equal_to_a_cold_extract` checks this after each step.

Each resolution records what it read (`resolver/deps.rs`, a thread-local recorder scoped to one `resolve_component` call):

| Dependency | Recorded by | Re-resolves when |
| --- | --- | --- |
addon-finds-the-component-by-its-export.md
addon-ignores-storybooks-cache.md
addon-prefetches-the-opening-story.md
anonymous-default-has-its-own-identity.md

The Storybook addon now finds the component a story imports by how its module exports it, without reading the module's source: a renamed export (`export { Inner as Card }`), a default export, and a sub-component attached to an export (`Menu.Item` beside `export default Menu`) each resolve to their own component. It no longer takes a file's only component for its default export, or a component whose display name matches the import when the module exports something else under that name; a story whose import names no component the module exports reports that the file has no such component, with the components it does have. A default export a call wraps (`export default React.forwardRef(Inner) as T`) is still read from the source when the module records no export for it.
---
npm/caliper-docgen-storybook: patch
---

The Storybook addon now starts in a real `storybook dev`. Storybook hands an addon's preset its own options together with the addon's, and its own `cache` (its file-system cache) reached the native session as the addon's `cache` option, which the session refused, so every story fell back to Storybook's own docgen with "could not start: Failed to convert napi value into rust type `bool`". The addon now reads `cache` only when it is a boolean you set.
---
npm/caliper-docgen-storybook: minor
---

When `storybook dev` starts, the Storybook addon now documents the opening story's component through Storybook's docgen service before a browser asks. That starts the docgen worker, the session and, with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, the checker, and stores the answer where the browser reads it, so the first story no longer pays the cold start: on a Chakra project, `Button`'s 1,137 props from the checker were in the browser before it asked, where they arrived 0.7 to 2.9 s after its request before (median 1.6 s). The new option `prefetchStories` (default `1`) sets how many first stories' components are documented, one after another; `0` turns it off. A story opened while a prefetch runs waits for it.
---

cargo/caliper-docgen: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: patch
npm/caliper-docgen: patch

docs/type-checker-integration.md:68:- **Names:** a symbol's `name` from the checker is its escaped name: a name that starts with two underscores has a third (`__size` arrives as `___size`, TypeScript's `escapeLeadingUnderscores`, so that it cannot collide with internal names such as `__call`). `rpc.rs` removes it when the answer is read, so every name downstream is the one the source writes.
docs/architecture/types-and-output-contract.md:261:`exported` says whether the component's module exports it: an exported declaration, an `export { X as Y }` or `export default X` of a local, or a sub-component attached to an exported component (`Parent.Sub = Sub`, `Object.assign(Parent, { Sub })`). Canonical output keeps unexported components; `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` omit them unless `--include-unexported` is passed, as react-docgen-typescript only documents exports.
docs/architecture/types-and-output-contract.md:263:`exports` (schema version 7, ADR 0027) is how the module exports it: one `{ name, members }` per way, where `name` is the export name (`default` for the default export, `Card` for `export { _Card as Card }`) and `members` the properties an attached sub-component is reached through (`Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default` with members `["Item"]`). A reader pairs a component by file and export, never by `displayName`: `_Card` and `Card` can be two components of one file, and `Item` can be a component's name and the name of another's attachment. An anonymous default export (`export default forwardRef(…)`) is named after its file and is no binding of that name, so a named export of that name beside it is another component: the default export is `E (default)` with exports `[default]` and the named one `E` with `[E]`, in whatever order the module writes them. A default export keeps the bare file name when no component of the file has it. A default export a call wraps (`export default React.forwardRef(Inner) as T`, `export default memo(forwardRef(Card))`) is an export of the component the call wraps, `Inner` or `Card`, unless the call builds a component of its own from its type arguments. A re-export (`export { Card } from './Card'`) is in no component's `exports`: the component belongs to the file that declares it. `exported` is `!exports.is_empty()`.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:35:- **Persisted export index:** following a name from a package's entry point to its declaring file walks re-export chains (chakra's `@ark-ui/react` is 1,434 mostly one-line `.d.mts` files, and shadcn's icon packages re-export 1,500+ names each), and opening files is the cost. The loader keeps one index file per package next to the parse cache: its re-export graph flattened to exported name → (declaring file, local name), covering `export *`, `export { a as b } from`, `export * as ns` and `import x; export { x }`, with cross-package names pointing into the other package's index. It is keyed by the package's real path and a hash of the resolver configuration, reused only while the package's `package.json` keeps its mtime and size, and discarded with the rest of the cache when the build changes. It is not the `DtsCache`: measured on the dependency closures, a warm `DtsCache` run was no faster than re-parsing in 6 of 7 cases (antd 80 ms warm against 45 ms with no cache), loading it cost 11 to 40 ms, and its 5,000-entry cap thrashed on shadcn's 6,217 files. Declaring files are parsed each run (parsing is 418 MB/s). Warm runs open no re-export stub: resolver calls inside dependencies fell from 4,842 to 603 on shadcn and from 2,171 to 572 on chakra, and loading cost 2 to 29 ms on the five projects. A cold run pays 10 to 55 ms more, and a package edited in place without touching `package.json` (patch-package) keeps a stale index until the cache is cleared.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:66:The augmenting file has to be in the loaded set. A project file is. A dependency file is when `load_dependencies` reaches it: `project_demands` adds a module-only demand (empty name) for every bare specifier a project file imports, whether or not a type from it is used, and `Loader::load_augmentations` reads the module's re-export closure (`export * from`, `export { x } from`, `export * as`; breadth first, at most `AUGMENTATION_SCAN_FILES` files per module) and loads each file with `React.`-qualified interfaces as a declaring file. TypeScript reads such a file whenever the program reaches it; this approximates the program by the re-export edges of imported modules. The answer per module, an empty one included, is kept in the layer and in the persisted index (`PackageIndex::augmenters`), so a run where no imported module augments React does not scan them again. The row is valid while the module's own `package.json` keeps its mtime and size and so do the `package.json` of every other package the search read a file from (the re-exports can lead into another package); an upgrade of any of them drops the row and the module is scanned again. Watch and lazy sessions treat the augmenting files as dependencies of every component that reads HTML attributes (`Dependencies::reads_augmentations`, plus each augmenting file in `Dependencies::files`): an edit to one re-resolves those components, and so does a project file that starts or stops declaring into the `React` namespace, since a file that is new, or that did not augment before, is in no recorded file list. A lazy session loads the module-only demands of every project file at start, because an augmentation reaches components in files that never import the package. Known gaps: files reached only through plain `import` edges, side-effect imports and `/// <reference>` directives are not followed, and `declare module "react/jsx-runtime"` (`JSX.IntrinsicElements`) is not merged.

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API of every published library crate for SemVer breaks against the last published version.
# The version only moves in the release PR, so a break is accepted when a pending minor or major changeset covers the
# crate. The CLI crate is a binary and has no library API.
semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    status=0
    for crate in caliper-docgen-core caliper-docgen-semantic; do
        if cargo semver-checks check-release -p "$crate"; then
            continue
        fi
        if grep -qsE "^cargo/$crate: (minor|major)$" .changeset/*.md; then
            echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for $crate"
            continue
        fi
        echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/$crate" >&2
        status=1
    done
    exit "$status"

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is

55-    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked
56-    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi
